thread:
Alex: FYI opened a small refactor PR that moves a shared dep into `runtime/lib` and updates packaging. not sure who needs to sign off — it touches both runtime and infra paths. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482
Morgan: Can you paste which files/dirs it touches? quick glance would help.
Alex: Sure — gist of it:
```
M runtime/lib/shared_utils.py
M runtime/BUILD.bazel
M infra/container/Dockerfile.runtime
M infra/packaging/runtime_package.yaml
```
Also CODEOWNERS has these rules currently:
```
/runtime/ @samir @runtime-team
/infra/ @infra-team @morgan
```
Jia: Hmm the CODEOWNERS rules are separate. Does the change actually modify infra logic or just packaging metadata?
Alex: Mostly packaging (container + package manifest). no behavior changes to runtime APIs.
Samir: I own runtime/ so I can review runtime code, but packaging under infra/ is usually Morgan's remit. If infra signs off on packaging, I'm fine approving the runtime side.
Morgan: I can take the infra side but need to confirm the Dockerfile tweak doesn't change base images. give me a minute to run the PR locally.
DeployBot: CI: All checks passed (unit tests, lint). Docker build step succeeded on CI image: runtime-build-2026-03-15
Alex: I tried not to change base images — only added one layer to copy `runtime/lib` and updated `runtime_package.yaml` to include the module.
Samir: Given that, I'm comfortable with approving runtime/* once infra confirms packaging. If Morgan approves infra/ I'll give my approval.
Morgan: Looks good to me — packaging change is sane and documented. small nit: swap order of COPY and RUN to leverage cache, pushed a tiny commit. I'll approve infra/ now.
Samir: Approved.
Alex: awesome, thanks both. Can someone merge after 24h if no rollback concerns? I'll keep an eye on flamegraph diffs after next deploy. :thumbsup:
Jia: tagging for visibility: @eng-sre in case rollback flags needed.
Morgan: will merge after CI passes again on the new commit.
Alex: thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.
